title: pvj-01
text:
Codelibrary(tidyverse)

workout_log <- data.frame(
  week = rep(1:4, each = 7),
  day = rep(c("Tuesday", "Tuesday",
              "Thursday", "Thursday", "Thursday",
              "Saturday", "Saturday"), times = 4),
  exercise = rep(c("Front Squats", "Flat Bench",
                   "Pull-ups", "RDLs", "Deadlift",
                   "Incline Bench", "Split Squats"), times = 4),
  category = rep(c("Lower Body", "Upper Body",
                   "Upper Body", "Lower Body", "Lower Body",
                   "Upper Body", "Lower Body"), times = 4)
)  # Rubin suggested seeing if I could put in my weights for the lift to see if I am progressing or not

ggplot(workout_log, aes(x = day, fill = category)) +
geom_bar() +
facet_wrap(~week) +
labs(title = "Weekly Baseball Lifting Routine", x = "Day of the Week", y = "Number of Exercises", fill = "Exercise Category")  # Owen was interested to see if using facet a different way could show a different kind of variation
